source.citation: J. O. Kephart, R. H. Pantell, B. L. Berman, S. Datz, H. Park and R. K. Klein, Phys. Rev. B 40, 4249-4263 (1989)
source.method: Sec. V D text, Figs. 16-17 captions and Tables I-II transcribed from the text layer and checked against 130 dpi renders of PDF pages 12-13 (printed pp. 4260-4261)

temperature: not stated (293.15 K assumed, as in checks/kephart_occupation.py)

beam.divergence_note: Table II average beam divergence inferred from the measured initial populations, not measured directly; Sec. V D says (100) is consistent with 1.8 mrad and (110) with about 2.5 mrad, the beam being visibly elliptical.

detector.type: Ge detector on the beam axis
detector.note: Collimation, solid angle and resolution are given in Ref. 6 (R. K. Klein et al., Phys. Rev. B 31, 68 (1985)), which is not in the Zotero library; a point forward detector is assumed. Yields are per sr, so the solid angle cancels.

normalization: Absolute flux from the random-orientation bremsstrahlung yield between 80 and 100 keV (Sec. IV). For thicknesses above 10 um the plotted fluxes are multiplied by exp[mu(E) Z] (absorption-corrected, open squares).
multiple_scattering_bound: Sec. V E: no perceptible broadening or asymmetry of the 1->0 peaks; the channeled in-plane multiple-scattering angle after 15 um is below 15 mrad (A < 4 in A sqrt(z/um) mrad), against 2.5 sqrt(z/um) mrad for unchanneled electrons projected on one dimension.

integrated_exponential_fits.units: Y(Z) = A (1 - exp(-Z / L)), A in photons/(electron sr), L in um; slope = A / L in photons/(electron sr um)
notes: Fig. 17(d) caption prints 0.046(1 - exp(-Z/17)); the plotted curve saturates near 0.0046 and the text slope 0.00027 x 17 um = 0.0046, so 0.046 is taken as a misprint.
Table I gives the (110) n = 2 length as 17 um after a parallel sum with the 120 um photon absorption length; the 17(b) fit itself uses 20 um.
Sec. V D gives the (100) initial population as 12%; Table II lists 11.6%.
Fig. 17(c) (3->2, ~6 keV) has no fit: detector efficiency is very small there.
Scatter: at 80-100 um the (110) 1->0 points span about 0.037-0.072 photons/(e sr) for different beam conditions; Table I lengths are quoted with about +-20% uncertainty.

line_energies_text_keV.note: Approximate values stated in the text (Secs. IV and V D), not fitted centroids.
